ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, if the periodic signal [see figure (a)] is input into the circuit composed of a 555 timer [see figure (b)] with \(V_{CC}=5\text{V}\), what is the duration of the high level of the output signal in one period?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure (a) gives the input periodic signal ui, which is a triangular waveform: it rises linearly from 0 V to +5 V, then falls linearly through 0 V, continues to -5 V, and then rises again; the figure marks the time positions of 5 ms and 10 ms, and the waveform slope magnitude is 2 V/ms. Figure (b) is a 555 timer circuit: pins 8 and 4 are connected to VCC, pin 1 is grounded, pins 2 and 6 are connected together and connected to input ui, pin 3 is output uo, and pin 5 is grounded through a capacitor, so this connection is equivalent to a 555 Schmitt trigger. Reasoning: VCC=5 V, so the two switching thresholds of the 555 are 2VCC/3=10/3 V and VCC/3=5/3 V. When input ui rises from 0 V to +5 V on the rising segment, the time to reach 10/3 V is t=(10/3)/(2 V/ms)=5/3 ms, and at this time the output flips to low level. Then the input falls from +5 V to -5 V, and the time to reach 5/3 V on the falling segment is t=2.5 ms+(5-5/3)/(2 V/ms)=25/6 ms, and at this time the output flips to high level. The next time the output becomes low occurs when the next period's rising segment reaches 10/3 V, namely t=10 ms+5/3 ms=35/3 ms. Therefore, within one period, the duration of the output high level is 35/3 ms - 25/6 ms = 15/2 ms = 7.5 ms.

method.method_draft: First describe the waveform and circuit from the image. Use VCC=5 V from the text to compute thresholds 10/3 V and 5/3 V. On the rising segment from 0 to +5 V, find the time when ui reaches 10/3 V; this is t = (10/3)/(2 V/ms) = 5/3 ms, so the 555 output becomes low. On the following falling segment from +5 V to -5 V, find when ui falls to 5/3 V; this is t = 2.5 ms + (5 - 5/3)/(2 V/ms) = 25/6 ms, so the output becomes high. The next reset occurs one period later at t = 10 ms + 5/3 ms. Therefore the high duration is from 25/6 ms to 35/3 ms, equal to 7.5 ms.
